models.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B
models.blurb: Tiny and quick. Great first test of your setup, and a draft model for bigger Qwen models.

models.name: Qwen3 0.6B
models.blurb: Tiny Qwen3 model. Mainly here as a draft model that speeds up bigger Qwen3 models.

models.name: Qwen3.5 4B
models.blurb: Surprisingly capable for its size. Fast on laptops with 8 GB or more.

models.name: Qwen3 4B 2507
models.blurb: Solid small model on a long-established architecture, so every app can run it. The best choice for comparing engines head to head.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.blurb: Google’s on-device model. Strong writing and multilingual chat in a small footprint.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.blurb: The sweet spot for 16 GB machines. Solid coding and reasoning.

models.name: Qwen3.6 27B
models.blurb: Best all-rounder for a 24 GB card. Dense, so every weight works on every token.

models.name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B
models.blurb: Reliable instruction follower with good tool calling. Plain attention, easy to fit.

models.name: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B
models.blurb: Mixture of experts with only 3B active per token, so it is very fast once it fits.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B
models.blurb: OpenAI’s open-weight reasoner, shipped natively in MXFP4. Nothing to lose by quantising.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
models.blurb: Google’s mid-size MoE. 4B active, strong writing quality.

models.name: gpt-oss 120B
models.blurb: The big one from OpenAI. Expert offload to RAM is what makes this run on a single GPU.

models.name: GLM-4.5-Air
models.blurb: 106B MoE with 12B active. Excellent agentic coder if you have the RAM.

models.name: Qwen3-Next 80B-A3B
models.blurb: Hybrid linear attention, so long contexts cost very little memory.

models.name: Qwen3.5 122B-A10B
models.blurb: Frontier-class open MoE. Needs a lot of RAM; the planner decides what lives where.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next
models.blurb: Huge sparse MoE built for speed. Verify llama.cpp support for your engine build before relying on it.
